messages:
samir: Pager fired for tenant tamarind-42 in prod (dedicated VPC pool). Tail latency p99 spiking to ~8s, p95 ~2s, small increase in 5xxs to 2.8%. Customer (Tamarind Inc) reporting timeouts on long prompts. Paging eng-oncall.
incident-bot: [pager] Severity: P2. Affected: tamarind-42 (dedicated). Auto-opened incident INC-7593. Linking oncall channel.
kevin: on it, grabbing logs + topology. Any recent rollouts for tamarind?
ryan: infra checked — no infra deploys in last 2h on that pool. I see a surge of long-sequence requests from a single origin IP range. Batching stats show very large batches forming (avg batch_tokens ~ 12k) for that tenant due to long prompts + high concurrency.
tess: customer says intermittent 503s during peak business hour, mostly long-completion jobs. They're on dedicated GPUs, pinned to pool dpool-7.
marta: sounds like max_batch_tokens is letting giant batches block the scheduler. For bespoke tenants we usually set `max_batch_tokens` lower and enable `tenant_shaper` so they don't monopolize the queue. What's tamarind's current override?
kevin: checking tenant override: `max_batch_tokens: 16384`, `scheduler_priority: 90`, `max_concurrent_batches: 8`. That explains it — huge batches.
samir: proposed immediate mitigation: reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 2048 and set `max_concurrent_batches` to 4 for tamarind-42, enable `burst_reserve: true` so other tenants don't starve if their bursts arrive. Also consider `queue_isolate: true` to move tamarind into a bespoke queue on dpool-7 if needed. Any objections?
marta: +1. Also enable `prefix_kv_cache` for the tenant if they often repeat prefixes — that'll reduce token work.
kevin: applying quick override (non-destructive) now. Command: 
```
curl -s -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/tenants/tamarind-42/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"max_batch_tokens":2048,"max_concurrent_batches":4,"burst_reserve":true}'
```
kevin: API returned 202 accepted. Override id: ov-9932. Pushing change to runtime via rollout job.
deploy-bot: Rollout job started for override ov-9932 -> target: dpool-7. 3 workers will pick up new config.
kevin: runtime logs (tail): 
```
[12:48:06] scheduler: loaded override ov-9932 for tenant tamarind-42
[12:48:08] scheduler: reducing candidate batches for tenant tamarind-42, updated max_batch_tokens=2048
[12:48:09] scheduler: max_concurrent_batches=4
```
ryan: metrics now: p95 dropped to 1.4s within one minute, p99 trending down — from 8s to ~3.4s so far. 5xx rate fell to 0.6%. Good sign.
samir: nice. Customer-side: Tess, can you update Tamarind Inc runbook about this and mention the transient impact?
tess: pinged customer via support channel, they saw fewer timeouts after 12:49. They want root-cause details and an ETA for permanent tuning.
marta: for permanent fix we should: 1) add tenant-specific scheduler profile template (profile: "heavy-long-seq") that defaults to lower max_batch_tokens and stricter concurrency, 2) enable adaptive shard-shepherding (auto-isolate if batch_token avg > X), 3) add synthetic eval to catch regressions for long prompts.
kevin: I'll open an RFC and schedule a canary for the profile on dpool-7. For this customer, propose permanent override: `max_batch_tokens: 4096`, `max_concurrent_batches: 3`, `scheduler_priority: 70`, `queue_isolate: true` — less aggressive than our emergency change but safer.
ryan: ops note: We should also add an alert: if a single tenant's avg batch_tokens > 8k for > 2m, auto-create a mitigation ticket and optionally apply a conservative override. Could automate with existing runbook.
samir: shifting on-call to june in 5 min. June, can you own follow-ups and verify no regression over next 2 hours?
june: ack — taking handoff. I'll watch p99 and 5xx for tamarind-42 and confirm with customer.
kevin: posting final audit: override ov-9932 applied at 12:48:06 UTC. Emergency rollback window 30m. If stable, I'll convert to permanent override ov-9932a per RFC-1218.
incident-bot: Incident INC-7593 updated: mitigation in place (config override). Severity lowered to P3.
june: 30m check-in — p95 steady at ~1.3s, p99 ~2.8s, 5xx ~0.4%. No new alerts. Customer confirmed normal operation for long prompts.
marta: follow-up action items: [ ] RFC for scheduler profiles (kevin), [ ] automation alert rule (ryan), [ ] tenant runbook update (tess), [ ] add test harness for long-seq workloads (eng-ml).
samir: thanks team. I'll close incident if no further regressions in 2h. Good cross-team coordination. :thumbsup:
kevin: one more note — we'll instrument `batch_token_distributions` per-tenant in the console so SEs can preemptively recommend knob changes.
june: closing loop — handing back to normal ops. If any regressions, please re-pager.
tess: I'll prepare customer-facing summary and attach to INC-7593.
kevin: RFC link (WIP): https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1218-timer/scheduler-profiles (will update with canary plan).
ryan: added automation ticket TKT-4246 for the alert rule.
samir: incident closed (no further activity). Thanks everyone.
